title: Signature Math Mapping — BCD (Binary-Coded Decimal)
description: How the Signature bitstring reads as BCD (Binary-Coded Decimal) (Base systems). In BCD each decimal digit 0-9 is stored as its own 4-bit nibble (e.g. 9 = 1001). Used in calculators and seven-segment displays.

fields.name: BCD (Binary-Coded Decimal)
fields.system: In BCD each decimal digit 0-9 is stored as its own 4-bit nibble (e.g. 9 = 1001). Used in calculators and seven-segment displays.
fields.mapping: Encode each decimal digit of the Signature's canonical measurements separately: apex (4.12, 4.92) becomes digits 4,1,2,4,9,2 -> six nibbles. Digit-exact, no binary rounding.
apply: 1. Write the measurement in decimal, e.g. segment length 1.37.
2. Convert each digit (1,3,7) to a 4-bit nibble: 0001 0011 0111.
3. Join with spaces. Reverse by reading each nibble as one digit.
